markscheme:
**(a)** $(x-3)(x+2)<0$; the parabola is below the axis between its roots: $-2<x<3$ **(M1)(A1)**

**(b)** $2x^{2}+5x-3\ge0\Rightarrow(2x-1)(x+3)\ge0$ **(M1)**: $x\le-3$ or $x\ge\tfrac12$ **(A1)**

**Common mistake:** solving the equation and stopping. Sketch the parabola to see which side of the roots satisfies the inequality.

prompt: Solve $3x^{2}-4x-2=0$, giving your answers in the form $\dfrac{a\pm\sqrt b}{c}$.
The equation $x^{2}+kx+(k+3)=0$ has two equal real roots. Find the possible values of $k$.
Find the values of $m$ for which the line $y=mx+1$ does **not** meet the curve $y=x^{2}+4$.
markscheme:
Intersections satisfy $x^{2}+4=mx+1$, i.e. $x^{2}-mx+3=0$ **(M1)**

No intersection $\iff$ no real roots $\iff\Delta<0$ **(R1)**: $m^{2}-12<0$ **(A1)**

$-2\sqrt3<m<2\sqrt3$ **(A2)**

At $m=\pm2\sqrt3$ the line is tangent to the curve ($\Delta=0$).
